title: Fewest Deletions To Put A Before B
statement:
The string s contains only the letters 'a' and 'b'. You may delete any characters you like.

Return the fewest deletions so that no 'b' comes before an 'a' anywhere in what remains. In other words, the result must look like some as followed by some bs (either part may be empty).

examples.why: Delete the leading b to get "aab".
Deleting the two b's is cheaper than deleting the three a's.
Delete the first b and the last a to get "aabbb". Deleting only b's costs 4 and deleting every a after the first b costs 3; the best fix mixes both.

hints: The final string has a cut point: everything kept to its left is 'a', everything kept to its right is 'b'. What does a given cut cost?
A cut costs (b's to its left) + (a's to its right). Trying all n + 1 cuts with prefix counts is already O(n).
One pass also works: keep bCount, the b's seen so far, and best, the answer for the prefix. On an 'a', either delete it (best + 1) or delete every earlier b (bCount).

explain.intuition:
Process the string left to right and keep best, the fewest deletions that make the prefix valid. A 'b' never hurts the prefix: it can always sit at the end. It only adds to bCount.

An 'a' after some b's forces a choice. Delete this 'a', which costs best + 1. Or keep it, which means every earlier 'b' must go, costing bCount. Take the cheaper one. Two numbers carry the whole state, much like a reducer that folds one character at a time.
pitfalls: Deleting only one letter type. In "baabbba" neither all b's nor all late a's is optimal.
Counting adjacent "ba" pairs. In "bbaaa" there is one such pair, but two deletions are needed.
Forgetting the empty-side cuts: keeping all a's or all b's are valid results too.

solutions.title: Try every cut, count each time
solutions.idea: For each cut position, count the b's on the left and a's on the right from scratch.

solutions.title: One pass with two counters
solutions.idea: On each 'a', either delete it or delete every 'b' seen so far, whichever is cheaper.

followups: Return the string that remains, not just the count.
The alphabet is 'a', 'b', 'c' and the result must be sorted. How does the state grow?
lcTitle: Minimum Deletions to Make String Balanced
